arxiv-1509-00368.title: A breakpoint detection error function for segmentation model selection and evaluation
arxiv-1509-00368.creator: Toby Dylan Hocking
arxiv-1509-00368.description: Abstract We consider the multiple breakpoint detection problem, which is concerned with detecting the locations of several distinct changes in a one-dimensional noisy data series. We propose the breakpointError, a function that can be used to evaluate estimated breakpoint locations, given the known locations of true breakpoints.

arxiv-2008-05999.title: Principal frequency of p p -sub-Laplacians for general vector fields Thanks: The first author was supported by FWO Odysseus 1 grant G.0H94.18N: Analysis and Partial Differential Equations and EPSRC grant EP/R003025/1. The second author was supported in parts by the MES RK grant AP08053051 and EPSRC
arxiv-2008-05999.creator: Michael Ruzhansky, Bolys Sabitbek, Durvudkhan Suragan
arxiv-2008-05999.description: Abstract . In this paper, we prove the uniqueness and simplicity of the principal frequency (or the first eigenvalue) of the Dirichlet p p -sub-Laplacian for general vector fields. As a byproduct, we establish the Caccioppoli inequalities and also discuss the particular cases on the Grushin plane and on the Heisenberg group. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 35P30, 35H99. 1.

arxiv-2103-06729.title: Search for a viable nucleus-nucleus potential for heavy-ion nuclear reactions
arxiv-2103-06729.creator: T. Nandi 1# , D.K. Swami 1 , P.S. Damodara Gupta 2,3 , Yash Kumar 4 , S. Chakraborty 1 , and H.C. Manjunatha 5∗
arxiv-2103-06729.description: Abstract We have constructed an empirical formulae for the fusion and interaction barriers using experimental values available till date. The fusion barriers so obtained have been compared with different model predictions based on the proximity, Woods-Saxon and double folding potentials along with several empirical formulas, time dependent Hartree-Fock theories, and the experimental results.

arxiv-2109-14948.title: From Motility-Induced Phase-Separation to Glassiness in Dense Active Matter
arxiv-2109-14948.creator: Matteo Paoluzzi, Demian Levis, Ignacio Pagonabarraga
arxiv-2109-14948.description: Abstract Dense active systems are widespread in nature, examples range from bacterial colonies to biological tissues. Dense clusters of active particles can be obtained by increasing the packing fraction of the system or taking advantage of a peculiar phenomenon named motility-induced phase separation (MIPS).

arxiv-2212-03257.title: A General Framework for Removing Point Spread Function Additive Systematics in Cosmological Weak Lensing Analysis A General Framework for Removing Point Spread Function Additive Systematics in Cosmological Weak Lensing Analysis – G.2
arxiv-2212-03257.creator: Tianqing Zhang, Xiangchong Li, Roohi Dalal, Rachel Mandelbaum, Michael A. Strauss, Arun Kannawadi, Hironao Miyatake, Andrina Nicola, Andrés A. Plazas Malagón, Masato Shirasaki, Sunao Sugiyama, Masahiro Takada Surhud More
arxiv-2212-03257.description: Abstract Cosmological weak lensing measurements rely on a precise measurement of the shear two-point correlation function (2PCF) along with a deep understanding of systematics that affect it. In this work, we demonstrate a general framework for detecting and modeling the impact of PSF systematics on the cosmic shear 2PCF, and mitigating its impact on cosmological analysis.

arxiv-2302-00702.title: High-redshift supermassive black hole mergers in simulations with dynamical friction modelling
arxiv-2302-00702.creator: Colin DeGraf, Nianyi Chen, Yueying Ni, Tiziana Di Matteo, Simeon Bird, Michael Tremmel, Rupert Croft
arxiv-2302-00702.description: Abstract In the near future, projects like LISA and Pulsar Timing Arrays are expected to detect gravitational waves from mergers between supermassive black holes, and it is crucial to precisely model the underlying merger populations now to maximize what we can learn from this new data.

arxiv-2310-14931.title: Topological Derivative for Shallow Water Equations
arxiv-2310-14931.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . Coastal erosion is a major and growing environmental problem that describes the movement of sand caused by tides, waves or currents. Several phenomena contribute to the significant advance of the sea. These include climate change, with rising sea levels due to the melting of ice at the Earth’s poles, the amplification of the tidal effect, leading to the transport of large masses of sand, storms, etc.

arxiv-2310-17897.title: Event Generation and Consistence Test for Physics with Sliced Wasserstein Distance
arxiv-2310-17897.creator: Chu-Cheng Pan, Xiang Dong, Yu-Chang Sun, Ao-Yan Cheng, Ao-Bo Wang, Yu-Xuan Hu, Hao Cai
arxiv-2310-17897.description: Abstract In the field of modern high-energy physics research, there is a growing emphasis on utilizing deep learning techniques to optimize event simulation, thereby expanding the statistical sample size for more accurate physical analysis. Traditional simulation methods often encounter challenges when dealing with complex physical processes and high-dimensional data distributions, resulting in slow performance.

arxiv-2404-03081.title: First-order PDES for Graph Neural Networks: Advection And Burgers Equation Models Thanks: Note : This work was performed for an undergraduate research project from May to August 2023.
arxiv-2404-03081.creator: Yifan Qu, Oliver Krzysik, Hans De Sterck, Omer Ege Kara
arxiv-2404-03081.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have established themselves as the preferred methodology in a multitude of domains, ranging from computer vision to computational biology, especially in contexts where data inherently conform to graph structures. While many existing methods have endeavored to model GNNs using various techniques, a prevalent challenge they grapple with is the issue of over-smoothing.

arxiv-2404-04475.title: Length-Controlled AlpacaEval: A Simple Way to Debias Automatic Evaluators
arxiv-2404-04475.creator: Yann Dubois, Balázs Galambosi, Percy Liang, Tatsunori B. Hashimoto
arxiv-2404-04475.description: Abstract LLM-based auto-annotators have become a key component of the LLM development process due to their cost-effectiveness and scalability compared to human-based evaluation. However, these auto-annotators can introduce biases that are hard to remove. Even simple, known confounders such as preference for longer outputs remain in existing automated evaluation metrics.

arxiv-2504-05969.title: Extension of derivations to forms
arxiv-2504-05969.creator: Manujith K. Michel, Chitrarekha Sahu
arxiv-2504-05969.description: Abstract . The problem of extending derivations of a field F F to an F − F- algebra B B is widely studied in commutative algebra and non-commutative ring theory. For example, every derivation of F F extends to B B if B B is a separable algebraic extension or a central simple algebra over F . F.

arxiv-2510-07128.title: jmstate , a Flexible Python Package for Multi-State Joint Modeling
arxiv-2510-07128.creator: Félix Laplante
arxiv-2510-07128.description: Abstract Classical joint modeling approaches often rely on competing risks or recurrent event formulations to account for complex real-world processes involving evolving longitudinal markers and discrete event occurrences. However, these frameworks typically capture only limited aspects of the underlying event dynamics.

arxiv-2602-02622.title: Discrete dynamical systems with scaling and inversion symmetries
arxiv-2602-02622.creator: Vaguiner Rodrigues dos Santos, Enrique Chipicoski Gabrick, Edson Denis Leonel, Iberê Luiz Caldas
arxiv-2602-02622.description: Abstract In this work, we investigate scale invariance in the temporal evolution and chaotic regime of discrete dynamical systems. By exploiting the close interrelation between scaling and inversion transformations, we formulate scale symmetry in terms of inversion symmetry. As applications of our approach, we determine fractal dimensions and compute Lyapunov exponents for paradigmatic dynamical systems using scaling and inversion symmetries.

in-a-glass-darkly.title: In a Glass Darkly
in-a-glass-darkly.creator: Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu
in-a-glass-darkly.description: Five tales of the occult detective Dr. Hesselius, including 'Green Tea' and 'Carmilla' — the founding collection of the psychic-detective story. Assembled from the three-volume Project Gutenberg edition.

pmc-11598014.title: Optimization of Communication Signal Adversarial Examples by Selectively Preserving Low-Frequency Components of Perturbations
pmc-11598014.creator: Yi Zhang, Lulu Wang, Xiaolei Wang, Dianxi Shi, Jiajun Bai
pmc-11598014.description: Achieving high attack success rate (ASR) with minimal perturbed distortion has consistently been a prominent and challenging research topic in the field of adversarial examples. In this paper, a novel method to optimize communication signal adversarial examples is proposed by focusing on low-frequency components of perturbations (LFCP).

pmc-11625125.creator: Neider Duan Barbosa Castro, Fabiola Sáenz Blanco, Francisco Zorrilla Briones, Evy Fernanda Tapias Forero
pmc-11625125.description: The study focuses on identifying key variables to develop a model for managing technological capabilities in the alternative energy generation industry in Colombia and Mexico. The objective is to identify critical factors that influence strategic decisions in this sector. Researchers MsC Neider Duan Barbosa Castro, PhD PD Fabiola Sáenz Blanco, Dr.

pmc-12593355.title: Comparative analysis of COVID-19 critically ill patients across four pandemic waves in Greece
pmc-12593355.creator: Stelios Kokkoris, Aikaterini Goufa, Dimitrios Tsilivarakis, Fotios Kavallieratos, Georgia Minatsi, Despoina Papadaki, Aikaterini Pranti, Spyros Zakynthinos, Anastasia Kotanidou, Christina Routsi
pmc-12593355.description: IntroductionThere is limited information about trends in mortality of intensive care unit (ICU) patients with Coronavirus Disease-2019 (COVID-19) throughout the entire pandemic period.AimWe compared the ICU mortality among the four consecutive waves of the pandemic, according to the virus variant predominance.MethodsThis is a retrospective study of prospectively collected data extracted from our COVID-19 clinical database.

pmc-12727817.title: Strategic environmental assessment—exploring connections between environmental and health issues
pmc-12727817.creator: Thomas B. Fischer, Ben Cave, Shiu Fung Hung, Tiago Rodrigues, Birgitte Fischer-Bonde, Ainhoa Gonzalez
pmc-12727817.description: In this paper, how changes to environmental aspects considered in strategic environmental assessment (SEA) can affect human health is explored, based on a comprehensive and systematic literature review. Whilst health is a key aspect for consideration in SEA, how it should be approached has remained subject to discussion.

pmc-13233335.title: The perception of quality of care and respect of human rights in mental healthcare facilities among users during and after the pandemic in Sardinia, Italy
pmc-13233335.creator: Elisa Cantone, Vanessa Barrui, Michela Atzeni, Giulia Cossu, Viviana Forte, Federico Contu, Stefano Lorrai, Alessandra Perra, Elisa Pintus, Haidy Rocio Oviedo Cordoba, Giulio Oppes, Felice Curcio, Rober Romero Ramirez, Shellsyn Giraldo Jaramillo, Massimo Tusconi, Cesar Ivan Aviles Gonzalez
pmc-13233335.description: BackgroundThe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has strongly challenged health systems, but Italian community mental health services, rooted in the Basaglia reform and the World Health Organization (WHO) QualityRights framework, may have preserved a high perception of care quality and respect for human rights.

pmc-13336696.title: De Novo Design of Membrane‐Targeting Antimicrobial Peptides Against Gram‐Negative Bacteria Using a Generative Artificial Intelligence Framework
pmc-13336696.creator: Jingxiao Yu, Da‐Wen Sun, QingYi Wei, Yibing Zhang, Jidong Tang, Hongbin Pu
pmc-13336696.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR), particularly Gram‐negative bacteria, poses significant challenges due to their robust outer membranes limiting antibiotic efficacy. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) show promising potential to replace traditional antibiotics. This study proposes a multi‐condition constrained directed generation framework guided by the AMP antimicrobial mechanisms for designing membrane‐targeting antimicrobial peptides (MTAMPs) against Gram‐negative bacteria.
